context:
Goal: a triage session on your Mac does triage's work, roadmap pushes included, with no word to type and no cloud session needed.
Problem (rule): the guard proves a session's tier only from cloud tags, which a Mac session has none of, so it refuses a Mac triage's roadmap push.
Based on (ruling): your note on 213, 2026-11-04 17:44 CST: no tier word, and not cloud-only.
Based on (read): the guard reads tags from get_session; a file Claude cannot write is the only other proof Claude cannot forge.
Departs from: main, where only cloud tags prove a tier — b adds a tier file that only your computer's setup writes; d adds a hand-off of roadmap pushes.
home: roadmap step local-triage-tier-proof; docs/debts local-triage-tier-proof (draft PR with batch runner 8)

lastAnswer.note: it'd have to be working on mac or windows if file version. else build nothing for now on this is ok too put this as a debt. Filed 07:48 CST Nov 5 as roadmap step mac-triage-tier-debt.

options.gain: Mac triage pushes the roadmap like cloud triage, with nothing to type.
options.how: The Mac install (session_start.sh) writes a tier file in a state folder the guard refuses Claude any write to; the triage launcher on your Mac sets it for that session only.
options.label: A tier file your computer writes
options.lose: One setup step per Mac, and a guard rule that keeps Claude out of that folder.

options.how: No proof file; the Mac session sends each roadmap change to a cloud or Mac triage that can prove its tier.
options.label: Mac triage hands roadmap pushes to any live triage
options.lose: A roadmap push waits when no provable triage is up.

reply: Build nothing now. The gap is filed as a debt: a triage on your Mac or PC cannot prove its tier, so the guard refuses its roadmap pushes. The fix, when it comes, is the tier file, and it must work on both Mac and Windows. Roadmap step mac-triage-tier-debt writes the debt record.
short: Mac triage: tier file from setup
title: A triage session on your Mac reads its tier from a file your computer's setup writes: build it that way?
why: Recommended: b. It meets both parts of your note: no word to type, and Mac sessions work on their own.
